newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: BA Cargo picks Maastricht as admin. centre.
newsitem.headline: BA Cargo picks Maastricht as admin. centre.

text.p: British Airways World Cargo is setting up its former trucking hub at Maastricht- Aachen airport in the southern Netherlands as an administration headquarters for its Western European airfreight operations, its business manager, Western Europe told Reuters.

In a telephone interview World Cargo's Henk van Ameijde said the company is well advanced with a plan which will see eight employees at Maastricht process all airfreight waybills for the airline's freight uplift operations from airports in Germany, Belgium, the Netherlands Switzerland and France.

Van Ameijde added that until a year and a half ago, World Cargo operated an extensive European trucking operation from Maastricht- Aachen, collecting consignments from airports or hub locations throughout Western Europe.
But ferry prices and the distances involved combined to make the operation uneconomic, he said.
The airline has since replaced the truck collection and delivery service with regular air links, using Boeing 737, 767 and 777 aircraft to ferry freight to Heathrow.
He commented: "The combined uplift operation can lead to as many as 3000 way bills a month, and it seemed sensible to have the administration of this centred in one location."
World Cargo's Maastricht-Aachen offices are developing a dedicated database to process the accounting data, he said.

There are savings to be made by having all administration located in a central office, with information electronically transmitted from a variety of locations, including Geneva, Paris, Dusseldorf, Brussels, Amsterdam and Frankfurt. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
